This will delete the Termux runtime environment (dependency packages and cache). Saves and server cores (worlds, plugins, configs) will be kept. "Confirm Delete" = delete then re-initialize automatically; "Force Delete" = thorough uninstall, re-install manually. This action cannot be undone.

This will directly delete the Termux runtime environment and all dependency files (Java, etc.). Saves and server cores (worlds, plugins, configs) will be kept, and it will NOT re-install automatically. Re-install manually when needed. This action cannot be undone.

This app needs to download the runtime environment (approx. 50MB) and server core (approx. 50MB) from GitHub. GitHub servers are overseas, and access from within the country may be very slow or even fail. Several solutions are provided below, listed in order of recommendation.
Solution 1: Switch Termux environment download source
This app includes 7 GitHub mirror sources (gh-proxy.com, ghproxy.net, etc.) that can automatically speed up GitHub downloads. Switch and re-initialize to take effect.
Select a mirror source (recommended: gh-proxy.com or ghfast.top)
Return to the \"Overview\" page, tap \"Delete Termux Runtime Environment\"
Wait for re-initialization, download speed will improve significantly
Solution 2: Switch dependency package download source (apt mirror)
Dependency packages such as JDK, wget, and frp are downloaded from the official Termux source, which may be very slow domestically. Switching to a domestic mirror can greatly improve speed.
Select a domestic mirror (recommended: Tsinghua TUNA or Alibaba Cloud)
Return to the \"Overview\" page, delete the runtime environment and re-initialize
Different ISPs have vastly different routing quality to GitHub. Switching networks may produce immediate results.
Try switching between WiFi and mobile data
If using WiFi, try switching to 5G/4G data network
Different ISPs have different base station routes, try China Mobile/Unicom/Telecom
Downloads are usually faster during early morning or off-peak hours
Use proxy tools to accelerate GitHub access. This is the most thorough solution but requires additional tools.
Launch a proxy tool on your phone (supports global or per-app proxy)
Ensure the proxy node has low latency (recommended: Japan, Singapore, or US nodes)
Return to this app to re-download or initialize
Note: Some proxy tools may intercept large file downloads. It is recommended to switch to PAC mode or whitelist this app
Solution 5: Download on PC then transfer to phone
If your phone network really doesn\'t work, you can download on a PC and transfer to your phone via a file manager.
Open the GitHub release page in a PC browser to download the required files
Place the Termux environment ZIP in the app\'s internal storage files/home/ directory
Place the server core JAR in the files/home/home/servers/{core name}/ directory
Restart the app, the environment will automatically detect existing files and skip downloading
During download, this app displays real-time download speed (e.g. 2.35 MB/s). Generally:
Very fast (direct connection or quality proxy)
Tip: If speed is below 100 KB/s or stuck for a long time, it means your current network has difficulty accessing GitHub. Please try the solutions above.
Download path: home/servers/{name}/server.jar (each core has its own directory)

MT Manager is a powerful Android file management tool that supports browsing app private data directories without Root.
📥 Go to MT Manager official website to download
Download and install MT Manager from the official website (agree to the user agreement on first launch).
Enter MT Manager\'s main screen, swipe right to open the side panel, or tap the menu icon in the top-left corner.
Find the \"Add local storage\" option in the side panel and tap it.
In the popup list, find and check \"MineServeMobile\", then tap OK.
Return to MT Manager\'s main screen. This app\'s entry will appear in the side panel — tap it to browse files.
Navigate to data → files → home → home → servers folder to see all Minecraft server files (including plugins, configs, world saves, etc.).
After modifying server configuration files, you need to restart the server for changes to take effect. Do not delete the world folder, or your saves will be lost.

This app includes a custom DocumentsProvider (MTDataFilesProvider) that exposes file operation interfaces for the data directory. MT Manager connects to this Provider through Android\'s standard file access interface, enabling direct reading and writing of this app\'s private data in MT Manager — no Root access required.

💡 Don\'t want to self-host? The \"Free FRP Platforms\" card below provides free frp services such as OpenFrp / ChmlFrp / StarryFrp / SakuraFrp: after registering an account, fill in the node address, port, and Token assigned by the platform into the frpc.toml configuration above, then tap \"Start Traversal\".

Simply put, it creates a \"tunnel\": your phone connects through frp to a server with a public IP, and others can access your phone by connecting to that server. It\'s like making a hole in the wall — people outside can see what\'s inside through the hole.
Rent a cloud server from Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, or Oracle Cloud (which offers free ARM instances). The cheapest one is enough — the key is having a \"public IP\".
Install frp server on your server

After logging into the server, search fatedier/frp on GitHub, download the corresponding version, extract it and edit the frps.toml file:
bindPort = 7000
auth.method = "token"
auth.token = "Set any password"
Then run ./frps -c frps.toml to start the server.
Fill in the configuration on your phone
Fill the server\'s public IP in \"frp server address\" above, port 7000, and the Token with the password you just set (must be identical to the server side).

Tap the \"Start Traversal\" button above, and the program will automatically install the frp client and connect to the server. The first time it will be installed automatically via apt, please wait a moment.
Tell your friends how to connect
After successful startup, give your friends the server\'s public IP and port (default 25565). Enter IP:25565 in Minecraft \"Multiplayer\" → \"Direct Connect\" to join.

The server\'s firewall must allow ports 7000 (for frp communication) and 25565 (for MC), otherwise connections will fail. It\'s recommended to set a Token password to prevent unauthorized connections.
bore is a minimalist TCP tunneling tool with a super simple protocol of only 3 message types. The mobile client is implemented in pure Kotlin, requiring no downloads and starting in seconds.
Like frp, you need a VPS with a public IP. Search ekzhang/bore on GitHub, download the bore binary, and run on the server: ./bore server
Fill the server\'s IP and port (default 7835) in the input box above, in the format your-vps.com:7835.
Tap the \"Start Traversal\" button, and the program connects directly to the bore server using your phone\'s network. No Termux needed, no downloads, starts in seconds.
After startup, the status card shows the public address (serverIP:port). Copy it and send to friends to paste in MC Direct Connect.
Pros: Extremely lightweight (~300 lines of code), starts in seconds. Limitations: TCP only, requires self-hosted server. Suitable for users seeking low latency and a lightweight experience.

Don\'t want to self-host? Register on any of the free frp platforms below to get started: fill in the node address, port, and Token provided by the platform into the frpc.toml configuration above to start.
